Trait indices of communities against null models

Source: R/trait_variation.R
community_index.Rd

Computes any index of the trait values of the individuals of each site (community), such as the variance, the range or a nearest-neighbour distance, and compares it with randomised communities.

Usage

community_index(
  individuals,
  index,
  traits = "trait",
  site = "site",
  species = "species",
  null = c("local", "regional.ind", "regional.pop", "regional.pop.prab"),
  n_perm = 99,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "less", "greater"),
  multivariate = FALSE,
  nperm = NULL
)

Arguments

individuals

Data frame with one row per individual.

index

Function of the trait values of a site (its first argument: a vector, or a matrix with multivariate = TRUE) and optionally of their species (an argument named species), returning a single number, such as stats::var, mnnd() or function(x, species) stats::var(tapply(x, species, mean)); or a named list of such functions, all computed on the same observed and randomised communities, such as list(variance = stats::var, MNND = mnnd, range = trait_range).

traits

Names of the columns with trait values.

site, species

Names of the columns with the site and the species.

null

Null model (see Details).

n_perm

Number of randomisations; 0 for the observed values only.

alternative

Direction of the test: "two.sided" (the default), "less" or "greater".

multivariate

If TRUE, the index receives all traits at once.

nperm

Deprecated; use n_perm.

Value

A data frame of class community_index with one row per site, trait (or "multivariate" with multivariate = TRUE) and index, and the columns site, trait, index (the name in the list, or the name of the function), observed, and with n_perm > 0 also ses and p; the attribute null holds the null values (randomisation x row), and plot() draws the tests. Individuals with a missing value are left out for that trait (for any trait with multivariate = TRUE).

Details

The null models follow Taudiere & Violle (2016), written from their description:

  • "local": trait values are permuted among the individuals of each site; the values of the site are kept and only their link with species is broken, so it is useful for indices that use species;

  • "regional.ind": each site receives as many trait values as it has individuals, drawn without replacement from all individuals of the data;

  • "regional.pop": each individual takes the mean of its population, and each site receives as many of these values as it has individuals, drawn without replacement from all individuals. The observed index uses the values of the individuals, so the null removes the variation within populations as well as the species composition of the site;

  • "regional.pop.prab": the index is computed on the means of the populations of each site (one value per population, observed and null alike), and each site receives as many population means as it has populations, drawn without replacement from all populations.

In all cases the individuals (or populations) keep their species, so an index with an argument named species, such as function(x, species), receives the species of the values of the site. With multivariate = TRUE the index receives the matrix of all traits of the site, and randomisations move whole rows, so that the traits of an individual stay together. Sites and species are matched by name, so the order of the rows does not matter. An index that the null model cannot change (for example stats::var under "local") gets ses = NA.

References

Taudiere, A., & Violle, C. (2016). cati: an R package using functional traits to detect and quantify multi-level community assembly processes. Ecography, 39, 699–708. doi:10.1111/ecog.01433

Examples

set.seed(1)
ind <- data.frame(site = rep(paste0("s", 1:5), each = 20),
                  species = sample(letters[1:4], 100, replace = TRUE))
ind$trait <- c(a = 1, b = 2, c = 3, d = 4)[ind$species] + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)
# range of trait values within sites, against draws from the whole region
community_index(ind, function(x) diff(range(x)), null = "regional.ind", n_perm = 99)
#>   site trait index observed         ses    p
#> 1   s1 trait index 3.155201 -1.79804612 0.12
#> 2   s2 trait index 3.695020  0.53805219 0.68
#> 3   s3 trait index 3.843434  1.13858880 0.40
#> 4   s4 trait index 3.297534 -0.97698903 0.42
#> 5   s5 trait index 3.579527 -0.02346576 0.94
# variance among the population means of a site
pop_var <- function(x, species) stats::var(tapply(x, species, mean))
community_index(ind, pop_var, null = "local", n_perm = 99)
#>   site trait   index observed      ses    p
#> 1   s1 trait pop_var 1.476106 4.219795 0.02
#> 2   s2 trait pop_var 1.577807 7.631109 0.02
#> 3   s3 trait pop_var 2.090731 7.206326 0.02
#> 4   s4 trait pop_var 1.661834 8.237044 0.02
#> 5   s5 trait pop_var 1.713591 4.415371 0.02
# several indices at once, on the same randomised communities
community_index(ind, list(variance = stats::var, MNND = mnnd, kurtosis = trait_kurtosis),
                null = "regional.ind", n_perm = 99)
#>    site trait    index    observed          ses    p
#> 1    s1 trait variance  0.96184073 -1.204549411 0.24
#> 2    s2 trait variance  1.01906139 -1.315648430 0.24
#> 3    s3 trait variance  1.55696893  0.955877885 0.34
#> 4    s4 trait variance  0.88096775 -1.394588992 0.16
#> 5    s5 trait variance  1.72488384  2.015358652 0.06
#> 6    s1 trait     MNND  0.08888870 -0.721103852 0.50
#> 7    s2 trait     MNND  0.11849284  0.847592936 0.46
#> 8    s3 trait     MNND  0.12324692  1.028942015 0.38
#> 9    s4 trait     MNND  0.04634544 -2.976977563 0.02
#> 10   s5 trait     MNND  0.09741112 -0.370322230 0.72
#> 11   s1 trait kurtosis -1.05229048 -0.007918248 0.90
#> 12   s2 trait kurtosis -0.10003062  3.187360206 0.06
#> 13   s3 trait kurtosis -1.23233713 -0.420626901 0.76
#> 14   s4 trait kurtosis -0.68087734  0.906284555 0.36
#> 15   s5 trait kurtosis -1.55901734 -1.373313414 0.02
